title: Clips without audio, or whose track query failed, can never be trimmed
claim: ClipPlayer.tsx:535 `const dirty = duration > 0 && mix.tracks.length > 0 && !sameEdit(...)` requires at least one track. stems.rs `tracks()` returns `in_file` (an empty list) when the file has no audio stream, and useClipMix.ts:163 turns a failed `clipTracks` call into an empty list (`.catch(() => undefined)`). Setup allows "no audio source" ("your clips are silent"); such clips, and any clip while ffprobe is unavailable (ffmpeg still downloading or failed), keep Save disabled forever. The editor then also says "This clip carries a single audio track" (ClipEditor.tsx:123), which is wrong when the query failed.
scenario: User chose "no audio source" in Setup (or ffmpeg is still downloading), sets a trim, and Save never becomes enabled.
fix: Use `!mix.loading` instead of `tracks.length > 0`, and show a separate "Tracks could not be read" message on error.

votes.evidence: src/components/ClipPlayer.tsx:535-538 `const dirty = duration > 0 && mix.tracks.length > 0 && !sameEdit(...)`; ClipEditor.tsx:225 Save `disabled={busy || !dirty || !inTauri}`, and save() is reached only from onSave (ClipPlayer.tsx:890), with no hotkey. src-tauri/src/muxer.rs:252,292-294: no WAVs means mix_filter returns None, so the clip is written with `-an` and has no audio stream. stems.rs:173-178 `if in_file.len() <= 1 { return Ok(in_file); }` then returns [] for such a file. useClipMix.ts:160-162 `.catch(() => undefined)` leaves tracks=[]. Setup.tsx:283-287 lets the user skip audio ('Without an audio source your clips are silent', 'Later, on the Audio page'). The backend has no such limit: edit.rs:402,665 accepts an empty list and writes `-an`. A second path: edit.rs:665 plus stems.rs:366 (a muted track gives -inf, which mix_filter drops) mean that muting the only track of a single-track clip without trimming writes an audio-less file and archives no original (edit.rs:304,311), so that clip is locked afterwards too. ClipEditor.tsx:121-125 shows 'This clip carries a single audio track' whenever !separateTracks, including when there are zero tracks or the read failed.
votes.corrected_claim: Holds as stated, with one change. The 'ffmpeg missing or still downloading' part matters little: edit::apply calls stems::tracks and ffmpeg itself (edit.rs:402,425), so Save would fail anyway without ffprobe or ffmpeg. In that case only the misleading 'single audio track' text is the real defect. There is also a path the reviewer missed: muting the only track of an untrimmed single-track clip and saving strips the audio for good, and the clip can never be trimmed or unmuted again.
votes.reachable_by: Ordinary use by the user. It happens to anyone who skips audio in Setup or turns every source off on the Audio page and then opens a clip to trim it, and to anyone who mutes the only track of a clip and saves. A failed ffprobe query is rarer (missing or corrupt tool download).
votes.fix_assessment: Gating on `!mix.loading` (plus a separate track-read error state) unblocks trimming silent clips, because the backend already handles an empty track list. Keep Save disabled, or show 'Tracks could not be read', when clipTracks rejected, since apply would fail the same way. Replace the 'single audio track' text with a no-audio message when tracks is empty.

A clip with no audio sources gets no audio stream: muxer.rs builds `wavs` only from snapshot.tracks (~150-200), `stems::mix_filter(&[])` returns None (stems.rs:332-334) and muxer.rs:293-295 pushes `-an`; `keep_stems = wavs.len() > 1` so no index is written. stems.rs:173-178 `if in_file.len() <= 1 { return Ok(in_file); }` then returns the empty list from ffprobe, commands.rs:983-990 passes it through, useClipMix.ts:159 sets tracks=[]. Query failure: useClipMix.ts:163 `.catch(() => undefined)` leaves tracks=[]; the effect only re-runs on `[clipId]` (168). ClipEditor.tsx:123 `{!loadingTracks && !separateTracks && (... "This clip carries a single audio track" ...)}` also fires for 0 tracks and for errors. The backend could trim such a clip: edit.rs:640-666 with an empty list gives filter None and `-an`, i.e. a valid audio-less trim.
votes.corrected_claim: The audio-less case is exactly as claimed: no audio source means no audio stream, so the track list is empty and Save stays disabled for good. A single-track clip saved with its only track muted also loses its audio stream (`-an`); if it was not trimmed, no original is kept, so it can never be edited again either. The query-failure case is overstated. Save comes back when the clip is reopened, because the effect is keyed on clipId. And while ffmpeg/ffprobe is missing, a save would fail anyway, because edit.rs run() needs both. The real problem in that case is the misleading 'single audio track' text and the missing retry.
votes.reachable_by: Any user who recorded with no audio source enabled (offered in Setup), or who muted the only track of an untrimmed single-track clip and saved. Also any clip opened while ffprobe is unavailable or fails (until the clip is reopened).
votes.fix_assessment: Swapping in `!mix.loading` alone is unsafe. After a failed query (tracks=[]) on a clip with a stored edit, sameEdit sees a length mismatch, so the clip shows as dirty with nothing changed. Saving then sends an empty mix, and stems::levels resets every track to 0 dB and unmuted, wiping the stored mix. The fix should keep an empty list from a successful query apart from an error, compare only the trim when the list is legitimately empty, and block a save (or send clip.edit.tracks) after an error.

title: A running Save/Undo-trim does not block paging, closing or deleting
claim: `save()` at ClipPlayer.tsx:547-582 (`resumeAt`, `veil.freeze`, `await applyClipEdit`, then in `finally` `setReload((n)=>n+1)` and `setJustSaved(true)`) runs while the keyboard handler (`n`/`p` -> `step`, Escape -> `close`), the Step buttons, Delete and the close button stay enabled. ClipPlayer.tsx:253 resets `justSaved` only when the clip changes, before the save finishes. Paging to clip B during A's save: B plays under A's frozen frame; when A finishes, `setJustSaved(true)` makes B show "Saved. That is how the clip sits in the folder now"; `setReload` re-creates B's `<video>` so B restarts; the editor shows "Saving..." for B and the progress bar stalls because the listener now filters on B's id. Closing during a save calls Clips.closePlayer, which runs `fileClip` while the edit job may be between ffmpeg and `swap_in`; deleting during a save runs `delete_clip` while `apply` runs. The core's render lock does not cover filing or deletion. (UI part confirmed; Rust races speculative.)
scenario: The user saves clip A (a re-encode can take minutes) and presses `n`; clip B is wrongly reported as saved, restarts, and shows a stalled progress bar. Closing or deleting during the save races `fileClip`/`delete_clip` against the edit job.
fix: While `saving || restoring`, disable step, close, delete and the shortcuts; alternatively key `saving` and `justSaved` by clip id and ignore results for a clip that is no longer shown.

Nothing checks `saving||restoring` outside save/restore/discard: step() :268-274 only checks bounds; keys :488-489 `n: () => step(1), p: () => step(-1)`; Escape :492-497 only checks fullscreen/askingDelete/exporting before close(); close button :680-682 and backdrop onClick={close} :650 have no disabled; Delete button :971-977 and Step buttons :987-999 (`disabled={index === 0}` / `index >= clips.length - 1`) ignore saving. :253-256 `useEffect(() => { setJustSaved(false); ... }, [clip?.id])` runs on paging, i.e. before A's await resolves, so A's later setJustSaved(true) lands on B; :633 `showSaved = justSaved && !dirty` -> ClipEditor.tsx:245-247 'Saved. That is how the clip sits in the folder now'. :287-290 resets resumeAt to null on clip change, so the reload (key={reload} :727) restarts B from 0/trim start. :303-314 progress listener re-subscribes with `update.clipId === clipId` for B, so A's progress is dropped while saving stays true (ClipEditor.tsx:230 'Saving...', SaveVeil :813-818 active over B with A's frozen still). Core: Clips.tsx:327-336 closePlayer -> `for (const id of seen) if (left.has(id)) void fileClip(id)`; commands.rs:745-768 file_clip -> filing::place (filing.rs:114-138, rename P->P' when game/favorite folder differs) with no edit::WORKING; WORKING (edit.rs:53) is taken only in run() :383 and discard_all_originals :198. apply_clip_edit (commands.rs:1003, async) reads clip once and edit::run uses `let target = PathBuf::from(&clip.path)` :393, temp beside it :422, swap_in -> replace_file(temp, target) :559; store() commands.rs:1310-1341 never rewrites path. delete_clip commands.rs:676-704 + clips.rs:315-323 remove clip file/originals/row without WORKING, while run() later rewrites target, note and thumbnail (edit.rs:452-479).
votes.corrected_claim: The UI part is exactly right. On the Rust side the races are real, not just speculative, but the window is narrower than 'between ffmpeg and swap_in'. If you close during a save, fileClip only moves A when A's folder has to change (favorite or game changed this session; filing.rs:120-123 otherwise returns Ok(None)). The window is the whole ffmpeg run for jobs that read the archived original instead of the clip file: a front cut on a clip that is already trimmed and still has its original (plan VideoSource::Original, edit.rs:298-300), or Undo trim (restore_plan, edit.rs:320-328). In those jobs P is not held open, so place() renames P->P' and sets the DB path to P'. swap_in then renames the render to the old path P. The DB ends up pointing at the stale pre-edit file and carries the new edit/duration/size, while the new file sits untracked at P (for a restore, the original store is also removed at edit.rs:570). For VideoSource::Clip jobs, ffmpeg holds P open. On Windows the rename then usually fails with a sharing violation and is only logged, leaving only the gap after ffmpeg exits. Deleting during a save lets delete_clip drop the row and files; run() then re-creates the clip file, the originals note and the thumbnail as orphans, and store() fails with 'clip not found'. Undo trim never sets justSaved, so the false 'Saved' message only follows Save; the restart and the stalled progress follow both.
votes.reachable_by: The local user, through the normal player UI. Save (or Undo trim) on clip A, then press n/p, click a Step button, press Escape, click the close button or the backdrop, or confirm Delete before the core returns. A re-encode or remux can take seconds to minutes.
votes.fix_assessment: The proposed fix works: disable step, close, delete, the backdrop click and the n/p/Escape shortcuts while `saving || restoring` (or key the saving/justSaved/progress state by clip id), and it removes every UI symptom. To be robust, the core should also make file_clip/delete_clip take edit::WORKING, or re-read the clip path before swap_in, so other windows such as the console cannot hit the same race.

That is how the clip sits in the folder now' (when B has no unsaved changes), its video element restarts once, the editor shows 'Saving…' and its progress stops moving, and A's frozen frame covers B while B's audio plays. B's own Save is blocked until A's job ends. The Rust races are real but small. Closing during a save only calls fileClip(A) from Clips.tsx (Dashboard does not file). While ffmpeg holds the input the move normally fails and is logged as a no-op (commands.rs:760-763), and tidy files it at the next start. The job can then still write the edited file, and on a first cut also an archived original, back to disk. store() then fails with 'clip not found', leaving undeleted orphan files and a notice, with no loss of user footage. title: Unsaved trim and mix are lost without warning on close or paging
claim: Closing and paging in ClipPlayer have no check of `dirty`: Escape, `n`/`p` or the close button drop a carefully set trim and mix, with only the "Not saved yet" line as warning. ShotViewer, by contrast, asks "Discard unsaved marks?". There is also no Ctrl+S save shortcut.
scenario: User sets a trim and mix, presses Escape or `n`; the edits are discarded without a prompt.
fix: Add a dirty guard (an inline "Discard changes?" chip, as ShotViewer has) for close, paging and delete, and a Ctrl+S save shortcut.

votes.evidence: src/components/ClipPlayer.tsx:488-498 key map `n: () => step(1), p: () => step(-1), Escape: () => { if (document.fullscreenElement) return; if (askingDelete) return; if (exporting) return; close(); }` - no `dirty` check. ClipPlayer.tsx:268-274 `step` calls onIndexChange directly; :156-196 `close` plays the exit and calls onClose; :684 close button `onClick={close}`; :656 backdrop `onClick={close}`; :942-956 Step buttons call step(). :286-295 on clip-id change `setTrim({ start: 0, end: 0 })`, and useClipMix.ts:141-161 re-inits the mix from the saved edit, so the work is gone. `dirty` (ClipPlayer.tsx:535-538) is only passed to ClipEditor, which shows 'Not saved yet' (ClipEditor.tsx:244-245). No ctrlKey/metaKey handling anywhere in ClipPlayer.tsx (grep). ShotViewer.tsx:379-386 routes Escape in draw mode through tryLeaveEditing (:580-583, asks 'Discard unsaved marks?') and only pages in view mode (:405-408).
votes.reachable_by: The user, in ordinary use of the main-window player (Clips gallery or Dashboard). Escape, n or p (single-letter shortcuts, ignored only in text inputs), the close X, the prev/next buttons or a click on the header backdrop all drop the edits. Nothing on disk is lost, only the unsaved trim and mix, and the panel says 'Not saved yet'. Delete is already behind its own 'Delete clip?' question, and after that the clip is gone anyway.
votes.fix_assessment: An inline 'Discard changes?' chip on close and paging when `dirty`, with Escape cancelling it as in ShotViewer, is sound. A guard on delete adds nothing because delete already asks and removes the clip. Ctrl+S is a nice-to-have, not a defect.

votes.evidence: src/components/ClipPlayer.tsx:162-196 `close` (no read of `dirty`) is reached from Escape (492-497: only fullscreen/askingDelete/exporting short-circuit), the close button (682 `onClick={close}`) and also a backdrop click (650 `onClick={close}`). `step` (268-274) just calls `onIndexChange(next)`; bound to `n`/`p` (488-489) and the ‹/› buttons (987-998). Trim and mix live only in React state: `useState<Trim>` (112), reset on clip change (287-296 `setTrim({start:0,end:0})`), and useClipMix's `setMix` (useClipMix.ts setTrack/reset) is never persisted until `save()` -> `applyClipEdit` (568). `dirty` (535-538) is only passed to ClipEditor, which shows "Not saved yet — ..." (ClipEditor.tsx:244-245). Callers add no guard: Clips.tsx:665-673 `onClose={closePlayer}`, `onIndexChange={openIndex}`; Dashboard.tsx:272-279 `onClose={() => setPlaying(null)}`. ShotViewer, by contrast, routes Escape through `tryLeaveEditing` and shows `question="Discard unsaved marks?"` (ShotViewer.tsx:380-386, 1078-1087). No Ctrl+S handler exists: the onKey map has no `s`, and lockdown.ts only preventDefaults Ctrl+S (WITH_CTRL contains "KeyS").
votes.reachable_by: Any user of the clip player (gallery or dashboard): one keystroke (Escape, n, p), a click on the backdrop/close button or the paging arrows throws away an unsaved trim and mix. Side note: Ctrl+N / Ctrl+P also page, because the handler matches on event.key alone.

Ctrl+S save would need an explicit ctrlKey branch in onKey (lockdown only cancels the browser default, so the event still arrives).

title: Any reload of the video element resets the unsaved trim via restoreTrim on loadedmetadata
claim: ClipPlayer.tsx:756-759 runs `restoreTrim(clip.edit, length)` and then `if (restored) setTrim(restored)` on every `loadedmetadata`, and ClipPlayer.tsx:799 retries a failed load with `setReload(n+1)`. So whenever the source changes under the open player or a load error triggers a retry, the unsaved trim is overwritten and playback restarts. Example: the user hearts the same clip in the console; Console.tsx:752 calls `fileClip`; the rename succeeds (the asset protocol opens files per request with Rust's default share flags, which allow deletion); the store reloads with the new `clip.path`, the `<video>` src changes, `loadedmetadata` resets the trim. A single transient load error does the same.
scenario: User trims a clip in the main player, then favorites the same clip in the console; the clip is filed/moved, the main player's video reloads and the trim is reset.
fix: Restore the trim only on the first metadata load for a clip id, or after save and restore (use a "trimRestoredFor" ref).

votes.evidence: src/components/ClipPlayer.tsx:747-759 onLoadedMetadata: `const restored = Number.isFinite(length) ? restoreTrim(clip.edit, length) : null; if (restored) setTrim(restored);` runs on every load with no once-per-clip guard. :531 `source = base && reload > 0 ? `${base}?v=${reload}` : base` with base = fileUrl(clip.path), so a new clip.path changes src on the same element and reloads it. :791-801 onError `if (loadFailures.current < 2) { setReload((n) => n + 1); return; }`. :580/:614 save() and restoreOriginal() always `setReload` in finally, also when applyClipEdit rejects (store.ts:586-591 rethrows without updating clips). Console path: Console.tsx:752 `if (playingId !== clip.id) await api.fileClip(clip.id);` only checks the console's own player. commands.rs:745-767 file_clip calls filing::place, then announce_change. filing.rs:76-77 favorite goes to the FAVORITES dir, :272 std::fs::rename with 5 retries. store.ts:302-309 clips-changed re-lists every clip. Clips.tsx:270-275 `playing` is mapped from live store clips, so clip.path updates in the player. Tauri 2.11.5 protocol/asset.rs:52 `File::open(path.clone())` once per request (std default Windows share mode includes FILE_SHARE_DELETE, and the handle is dropped after the response), so nothing blocks the rename. useClipMix only rebinds on bindKey and does not reset the mix, so only the trim is lost.
votes.corrected_claim: The mechanism is right: every loadedmetadata re-applies the saved trim. Only the trim is reset; the mix sliders survive. The example scenario works but is uncommon. It needs the main-window player to stay open (it stays mounted while hidden) and the user to heart the same clip in the in-game console. Depending on timing, the next range request to the old path can fail first. The retry then also fails and leaves the player showing 'File not found', because `broken` is never cleared when the path changes. The reviewer missed a more likely trigger: a save that fails. save() always remounts the element in `finally`, and the store has not updated clip.edit, so the trim the user just tried to save goes back to the old saved one and the 'Not saved yet' hint disappears.
votes.reachable_by: The user. Most likely through a failed Save in the player (ffmpeg error, disk full, file locked). Less often by hearting the clip that is open in the main window from the in-game console (Console.tsx:752). Rarely by a media load error after metadata had loaded. No remote party can trigger it, and only unsaved UI state is lost.
votes.fix_assessment: A 'trimRestoredFor' ref keyed by clip id is the right shape. It has to be re-armed only after a successful save or restore, when the file length really changed, and not after a failed save or a path-only reload. It should come with clearing `broken` when clip.path changes, or the console-move race still strands the player on 'File not found'.

votes.evidence: src/components/ClipPlayer.tsx:749-759 onLoadedMetadata: `const restored = Number.isFinite(length) ? restoreTrim(clip.edit, length) : null; if (restored) setTrim(restored);` and restoreTrim (1033-1038) never returns null, so every metadata load overwrites `trim` with the stored edit (or the whole clip). Reloads: onError retry 799-801 `if (loadFailures.current < 2) { setReload((n) => n + 1); return; }` (new `key={reload}` element, 727). Source tracks live store data: `const base = clip ? fileUrl(clip.path)` (522) -> `src={source}` (729); Clips.tsx:270-275 maps the playlist onto live store clips; store.ts:302-309 reloads all clips on `clips-changed`. Console.tsx:743-752 hearts and then `if (playingId !== clip.id) await api.fileClip(clip.id);` (playingId is the console's own player and knows nothing of the main window). commands.rs:745-770 file_clip -> filing::place -> move_file (filing.rs:269-285, `std::fs::rename` with retries) -> `lib.set_path` + `announce_change`. Tauri asset protocol opens the file per request with `std::fs::File::open` (tauri-2.11.5/src/protocol/asset.rs:52) and builds an in-memory body, so no long-lived handle blocks the rename. Another trigger within the main window alone: save() (567-581) calls `setReload` in `finally` even when applyClipEdit throws (store.ts:589-595 rethrows), so a failed save also reloads, and the trim falls back to the old `clip.edit`.
votes.reachable_by: A user with a clip open and trimmed in the main window who hearts the same clip in the in-game console (the Console.tsx comment itself expects the main window to be playing it). Also any transient media load error, and any failed save (e.g. the file is locked), which resets the trim to the previously saved state. Playback also restarts at 0 or at the stored start.

Separately, the claim that a rename succeeds while the file plays rests on Rust std's Windows default share mode (FILE_SHARE_DELETE), which is documented but could not be read in source here; the failed-save and retry paths do not depend on it.

title: Friends.tsx swallows errors
claim: Friends.tsx:78 swallows errors with `.catch(() => {})`, so failures are never shown.
scenario: A friends action fails and the user gets no indication.
fix: Show the error via a toast or `lastError` instead of swallowing it.

votes.evidence: src/console/Friends.tsx:76-78 `const run = (action: Promise<void>) => { setBusy(true); action.catch(() => {}).finally(() => setBusy(false)); };`, used for `friendsApi.remove(user.id)` (l.89) and `friendsApi.accept(user.id)` (l.96). Both commands really fail with user-relevant messages and do not notify themselves. friends.rs:242-252 `request(...).await?; refresh(&app, false).await`. friends.rs:755-767 `Err("Not signed in.")` / `"The friends server is not reachable right now."`. friends.rs:782-786 returns the server's error text or `The friends server answered {status}.`. The main-window equivalent reports them: src/routes/Friends.tsx:276 `action.catch(report).finally(() => setBusy(false));`.
votes.reachable_by: A local user accepting or declining a friend request from the in-game console while the friends server is unreachable, returns an error, or the session token is invalid. On 401, sign_out_locally (friends.rs:768-770) does flip the panel to the sign-in text, so that one case gives indirect feedback.
votes.fix_assessment: Correct and easy. Pass the console's existing `say` helper (Console.tsx:252) into FriendsPanel/Request and call it in the catch, matching what routes/Friends.tsx does with `report`.

title: Dashboard player never files favorites on close
claim: The dashboard's ClipPlayer never files favorites when it closes; the gallery (Clips.tsx) does that in `closePlayer`, so behaviour differs between the two players.
scenario: The user favorites a clip in the dashboard player and closes it; the clip is not filed the way it would be when closed from the gallery.
fix: Reuse the Clips.tsx playlist/close logic (including `closePlayer` filing) through a shared hook.

votes.evidence: src/routes/Dashboard.tsx:272-279 `<ClipPlayer clips={recent} ... onClose={() => setPlaying(null)} onDelete={deleteClip} .../>`: closing only clears state, no fileClip. Gallery: src/routes/Clips.tsx:327-336 `closePlayer` runs `for (const id of seen) if (left.has(id)) void fileClip(id);` over every clip in `touched`. ClipPlayer itself never files: src/components/ClipPlayer.tsx:938-952, comment "The file only moves into the favorites folder on close ... The gallery takes care of it." then `onClick={() => void setFavorite(clip.id, !clip.favorite)}`. Backend set_clip_favorite (src-tauri/src/commands.rs:713-727) only writes the DB; the only Rust callers of filing::place are file_clip (commands.rs:752) and the startup filing::tidy (src-tauri/src/lib.rs:1229).
votes.corrected_claim: Accurate, and a bit wider than stated: the dashboard player never files anything on close, so neither a favorite toggle nor a game change made in its editor moves the file. The file stays put until the next app start (filing::tidy at lib.rs:1229) or until the clip is opened and closed in the gallery. Nothing is lost; only the folder layout lags.
votes.reachable_by: Any user who opens one of the three 'Latest clips' on the dashboard, hearts it or changes its game in the player, then closes it.
votes.fix_assessment: Sound. Either give Dashboard the same touched-set and close logic (a shared hook works), or have ClipPlayer report the clips it showed when it closes so every host files them the same way.

title: Trim tolerance mismatch: UI says dirty/"Saved" for an end cut the core ignores
claim: ClipPlayer.tsx:1069 compares with `Math.abs(x - y) <= 50` while edit.rs:43 uses `EDGE_TOLERANCE_MS: u64 = 250`. Trimming 60-250 ms off the end enables Save; the core treats it as uncut, and the reload restores the full range, while the UI said "Saved".
scenario: User trims 200 ms off the end and saves; the UI reports "Saved" but the file is unchanged and the trim resets.
fix: Share one tolerance (250 ms) for `dirty`, the "trimmed" flag and the core.

votes.evidence: src/components/ClipPlayer.tsx:1069 `const near = (x, y) => Math.abs(x - y) <= 50;` drives `dirty` (ClipPlayer.tsx:535-538), and Save is enabled on `!dirty` (ClipEditor.tsx `disabled={busy || !dirty || !inTauri}`). Core: src-tauri/src/edit.rs:43 `const EDGE_TOLERANCE_MS: u64 = 250;`, edit.rs:283-285 `let cuts_front = start > EDGE_TOLERANCE_MS; let cuts_back = end + EDGE_TOLERANCE_MS < clip_duration_ms; ... absolute_end = offset + if cuts_back { end } else { clip_duration_ms };`. After the run, commands.rs:1327-1331 stores `ClipEdit { start_ms: 0, end_ms: applied.duration_ms, tracks }`. On reload, onLoadedMetadata calls restoreTrim(clip.edit, length) (ClipPlayer.tsx:756-759), which gives the full range. Then dirty is false and `showSaved = justSaved && !dirty` (ClipPlayer.tsx:633) shows "Saved. That is how the clip sits in the folder now".
votes.corrected_claim: Mechanism correct. Two details: (1) the file is not literally untouched. ffmpeg still rewrites it at full length (video stream-copied, audio remixed), so any mix change is applied and only the trim is dropped. (2) The start has the same gap: a start trim of 51-250 ms makes the clip dirty, but cuts_front is false, so it is also ignored and resets to 0 after save.
votes.reachable_by: A user who drags or marks the end (or start) handle 51-250 ms in from the edge and presses Save.
votes.fix_assessment: Sound: use one 250 ms tolerance for `sameEdit`/`dirty`, for the `trimmed` flag (ClipEditor.tsx:85 uses 0.05 s) and for the core. Alternatively, snap handles within 250 ms of an edge to that edge, so the UI never shows a cut the core will drop.

title: Solo is a listening aid in the UI but is saved as mutes
claim: useClipMix.ts:391-401 builds the saved state with `muted: !audible(state, anySolo)`, so soloing a track and pressing Save permanently mutes every other track in the file (recoverable because stems remain, but surprising).
scenario: User solos the game track to check something, presses Save, and the saved file has all other tracks muted.
fix: Exclude solo from the saved state and from `dirty`, or label it clearly ("Solo is saved as mute").

votes.evidence: src/lib/useClipMix.ts:386-399 doc comment "Solo does not exist there — it is resolved into mutes here." `const anySolo = ...some(state => state.solo); return tracks.map(track => ({ index, gainDb: state.gainDb, muted: !audible(state, anySolo) }))`. audible (useClipMix.ts:19-21) is `anySolo ? state.solo : !state.muted`. ClipPlayer.tsx:530-538 builds `current.tracks = mix.toRequest()`, so a solo alone makes `dirty` true. save() sends `current.tracks` (ClipPlayer.tsx:568). After reload, initialMix (useClipMix.ts:27-42) restores `muted` and sets `solo: false`. The other tracks therefore come back muted, with no solo shown.
votes.corrected_claim: Behaviour is as claimed, but it is a deliberate, documented design (useClipMix.ts:386-390), not an accident. The UI also flags it: soloing enables Save and shows "Not saved yet — the file in the folder is still a different one." It is recoverable, because the stems are kept untrimmed and are never replaced (edit.rs invariant 1), so unmuting and saving again remixes them.
votes.reachable_by: A user who solos a track in the clip editor and then presses Save (or saves another change while a solo is still on).
votes.fix_assessment: A labelling fix ('Solo is saved as mute') keeps the current design. Leaving solo out of toRequest/dirty would change it: 'Solo game audio, Save' would no longer produce a game-only clip, which some users may rely on. Product call.

title: Dragging a trim handle re-renders the whole player and editor on every pointer move
claim: PlayerControls.tsx:146 calls `onTrim(...)` on every `pointermove`, which calls `setTrim` in ClipPlayer; each change re-renders ClipPlayer, ClipEditor, ClipMeta, Tags and all TrackRows, and tears down and re-creates the rAF effect (deps `[playing, trim.start, trim.end, paint]`) and the keydown listener. The authors note WebView2 drops video frames when React renders at frame rate. The drag also does not handle `pointercancel` or use `setPointerCapture`.
scenario: User drags a trim handle during playback; video frames drop due to frame-rate React renders.
fix: Keep the trim in a ref during the drag and paint the handles directly (as for the playhead), commit on `pointerup`; read trim from a ref inside the rAF loop and key handler; handle `pointercancel` and use `setPointerCapture`.

votes.evidence: src/components/ui/PlayerControls.tsx:139-163: `const move = (moved: PointerEvent) => { ... onTrim(which === "start" ? {...} : {...}); }; window.addEventListener("pointermove", move); window.addEventListener("pointerup", up);`. There is no pointercancel and no setPointerCapture. onTrim is `setTrim` (ClipPlayer.tsx:843, 880, 910), so ClipPlayer re-renders and passes `trim` to ClipEditor. ClipEditor, ClipMeta, Tags and TrackRow are not memoized (the only memo( in src/components is ShotAnnotate.tsx:566). The rAF effect has deps `[playing, trim.start, trim.end, paint]` (ClipPlayer.tsx:379). The keydown effect lists `trim.start, trim.end` (ClipPlayer.tsx ~512-525). The authors' note at ClipPlayer.tsx:331-335 says 60 renders/s made WebView2 drop video frames.
votes.corrected_claim: The code facts all hold. That video frames actually drop during a drag is inferred from the authors' playback note and was not measured. Tearing down and re-creating the rAF loop costs little; the real cost is the React render on every move. Without a pointercancel handler, a cancelled touch or pen drag (no pointerup) leaves the window listeners attached, and the handle then follows plain hover moves until the next pointerup. Mouse use on Windows rarely hits this.
votes.reachable_by: A user who drags a trim handle, especially during playback. The pointercancel case needs touch or pen input.
votes.fix_assessment: Sound. Hold the trim in a ref during the drag, paint handles and veils directly, commit with setTrim on pointerup, and read trim from a ref in the rAF tick and key handler. Add pointercancel cleanup. setPointerCapture is optional, since the window listeners already track moves outside the bar.

title: Tauri event listener leak in ClipPlayer when cleanup runs before listen() resolves
claim: ClipPlayer.tsx:303-314 uses `.then((off) => { unlisten = off; }); return () => unlisten?.();`. If cleanup runs before `listen()` resolves (StrictMode, which `main.tsx` uses, or fast paging), the listener is never removed. ExportDialog.tsx:84-95 does this correctly.
scenario: User pages quickly through clips; listeners accumulate and keep firing for old clips.
fix: Add a `useTauriEvent(name, cb)` hook with a `cancelled` flag and use it everywhere.

votes.evidence: src/components/ClipPlayer.tsx:305-313: `let unlisten; void events.onClipProgress(...).then((off) => { unlisten = off; }); return () => unlisten?.();` -- no cancelled flag, so if cleanup runs first the later-resolved `off` is stored and never called. listen() is async: node_modules/@tauri-apps/api/event.js:71-82 `return invoke('plugin:event|listen', {...}).then((eventId) => async () => _unlisten(event, eventId))`, and the handler is registered via transformCallback before resolution. src/main.tsx:12 wraps the app in React.StrictMode, so the dev mount->cleanup->mount always hits this. Contrast ExportDialog.tsx:80-96 (`if (cancelled) unlisten(); else off = unlisten;`) and the comment in Toasts.tsx:37-39 describing exactly this bug.
votes.reachable_by: Always in development (StrictMode double-mount leaks one listener per ClipPlayer mount); in production only when clipId changes or the player unmounts within one plugin:event|listen IPC round trip (very fast paging with n/p or the step buttons, or an immediate close). The leaked listener stays registered for the window's lifetime but only calls setWriteProgress for its old clipId (a same-value update if that clip is saved again, a no-op after unmount), so the visible effect is a leaked IPC listener rather than wrong UI.
votes.fix_assessment: Correct: a cancelled flag (call `off()` if already cancelled), ideally factored into a shared useTauriEvent hook since the same pattern already exists in ExportDialog, Toasts and Overlay.

title: Waveform CSS url() is unquoted
claim: PlayerControls.tsx:185 ``backgroundImage: `url(${waveform})` `` leaves the URL unquoted. `convertFileSrc` uses `encodeURIComponent`, which leaves `(` and `)` unescaped, so a path containing parentheses breaks the declaration.
scenario: A Windows profile such as `C:\Users\Max (Work)\...` makes the background-image declaration invalid and the waveform never shows.
fix: Write `` `url("${waveform}")` ``.

votes.evidence: src/components/ui/PlayerControls.tsx:185 ``backgroundImage: `url(${waveform})` ``. waveform = fileUrl(path) (ClipPlayer.tsx:321) -> convertFileSrc -> tauri-2.11.5/scripts/core.js:15-17 `const path = encodeURIComponent(filePath); return ... `${protocolScheme}://${protocol}.localhost/${path}``. encodeURIComponent leaves `( ) ' ! * ~` unescaped. The path is config::data_dir()/preview/<sanitized id>_wave.png (preview.rs:16-18,37; config.rs:10-12 `dirs::data_dir().join("ClippiBoy")`), i.e. %APPDATA%\ClippiBoy\preview\..., so only the profile part can carry such characters. Per CSS Syntax 'consume a url token', an unquoted URL containing `(`, `'` or `"` becomes a bad-url-token and an embedded `)` ends it early, so the declaration is invalid and React's `style.backgroundImage = ...` assignment is silently dropped.
votes.reachable_by: Any Windows user whose roaming AppData path contains `(`, `)` or `'`: local account names like `Max (Work)` or `O'Brien` (both allowed in Windows user names), or a redirected AppData folder. The waveform silently never appears in the player timeline; nothing else breaks.
votes.fix_assessment: Quoting fixes it: `url("${waveform}")` is safe because encodeURIComponent turns `"` and `\` into %22 and %5C, and Windows paths cannot contain `"` anyway. JSON.stringify(waveform) inside url() would work just as well.

title: Scrubber slider lacks own key handling and live ARIA values
claim: The scrubber (PlayerControls.tsx:162-178) is `role="slider"` with `tabIndex={0}` but has no key handling of its own (it relies on the global arrow keys). `aria-valuenow` is a percentage that is not updated while playing (the rAF loop writes the DOM directly), and there is no `aria-valuetext`.
scenario: A screen-reader user focuses the scrubber and hears a stale percentage with no time text.
fix: Give the scrubber arrow keys and a time text (`aria-valuetext`).

votes.evidence: src/components/ui/PlayerControls.tsx:162-178: `role="slider" aria-label="Position" aria-valuenow={Math.round(progress)} aria-valuemin={0} aria-valuemax={100} tabIndex={0} onClick={...}` -- no onKeyDown and no aria-valuetext. progress is `(time / duration) * 100` (ClipPlayer.tsx:637), and `time` is set only on pause, seeked, ended, or timeupdate while paused (ClipPlayer.tsx:742-748 `if (e.currentTarget.paused) setTime(...)`), while the rAF loop (:357-379, paint :344-352) writes width, left and textContent straight into the DOM. So aria-valuenow freezes at the start-of-playback value. Keys come only from the window keydown handler (ClipPlayer.tsx:475-476 ArrowRight/ArrowLeft seek +/-5 s; Console.tsx:1274-1275 the same).
votes.reachable_by: Screen-reader users who focus the scrubber in the ClipPlayer or the console player while a clip plays. Arrow keys do work through the global handler, and each keyboard seek updates aria-valuenow through onSeeked, so the gaps are the stale value during playback and the bare percentage with no time text.
votes.fix_assessment: Adding aria-valuetext (e.g. `clock(time) of clock(duration)`) and updating the ARIA values at a throttled rate, or on focus, during playback is correct. A local onKeyDown is optional, since the global handler already serves a focused div.

title: Track mute/solo buttons have confusing or missing accessible names
claim: The track mute buttons flip both their label and `aria-pressed` (double state change), and the Solo buttons have no track context in their accessible name.
scenario: A screen-reader user hears ambiguous "Solo" buttons and contradictory mute state announcements.
fix: Keep a stable label with `aria-pressed`, and include the track name in Solo labels.

votes.evidence: src/components/ClipEditor.tsx:339-342 `<button aria-label={state.muted ? `Unmute ${label}` : `Mute ${label}`} aria-pressed={state.muted}`: when the track is muted, the button is announced as "Unmute Game, toggle button, pressed". The name and the pressed state both flip, so a pressed "Unmute" reads as if unmute were on. ClipEditor.tsx:362-373 `<button aria-pressed={state.solo} ...>Solo</button>` has no aria-label, so every row's solo button has the same accessible name, "Solo", with no track name. The track label is only a sibling span (line 360).
votes.reachable_by: Screen-reader users in the clip editor's Audio tracks section whenever a clip has separate tracks (one TrackRow per track).
votes.fix_assessment: Correct. Use a stable aria-label `Mute ${label}` with aria-pressed={state.muted}, and add aria-label={`Solo ${label}`} to the solo button while keeping the visible text "Solo".

title: Space on a focused button toggles playback instead of activating the button
claim: In the player, pressing Space while a button has focus toggles playback (global shortcut) instead of activating the focused button.
scenario: A keyboard user tabs to the Save button and presses Space; playback toggles and Save is not triggered.
fix: Skip the global Space shortcut when a button or other interactive control is focused.

votes.evidence: src/components/ClipPlayer.tsx:463-469 skips only text inputs (`target instanceof HTMLInputElement && target.type !== "range"`) and textareas. A focused <button> falls through to `" ": toggle` (line 471), then `event.preventDefault(); ... handler();` (lines 501-503) in a window keydown listener (line 505). The Save button (ClipEditor.tsx:224-231, a plain <button> through ui/Button.tsx:34-47) has no keydown handling of its own. Cancelling keydown for Space stops Chromium/WebView2 from arming the button, so no click fires on keyup and playback toggles instead. Enter is not in the handler map and still activates buttons.
votes.reachable_by: Keyboard users in the clip player who press Space on any focused button: Save, Start here/End here, Mute/Solo, the trim handles, Favorite, Delete and so on. Enter still works.
votes.fix_assessment: Correct. Skip the shortcut when event.target is a button, [role=button], [role=switch], select, or similar (or check `target.closest('button, [role=button], select, a')`), at least for Space. The same pattern also takes Arrow/Home/End away from the focused volume and track sliders, which may deserve the same treatment.

title: Setup step dots put aria-label on a plain div with no role
claim: The Setup step dots carry `aria-label` on a plain `div` with no role, so the label is not reliably exposed.
scenario: Screen readers ignore the step indicator label.
fix: Give the element an appropriate role (or use visually hidden text).

votes.evidence: src/components/Setup.tsx:199 `<div className="flex items-center gap-1.5" aria-label={`Step ${step + 1} of ${steps.length}`}>` has no role. Its children (lines 200-207) are empty decorative <span>s with no text. A div maps to the generic role, on which ARIA 1.2 prohibits naming. Screen readers generally do not announce aria-label on generic containers, and no text inside the element carries the step position.
votes.reachable_by: Screen-reader users going through the first-run Setup flow. The step position is not exposed (each step's title still is).
votes.fix_assessment: Correct. Use role="img" (or role="group"/"status") with the aria-label, or put visually hidden text such as Step 2 of 5 inside and aria-hidden on the dots.

title: REC badge blink composites at 60 fps on the CPU for the whole recording
claim: The REC badge uses `cb-rec-blink 1.4s infinite` (overlay.css:321), a smooth animation that composites at 60 fps on the CPU for the whole recording.
scenario: During a long manual recording, the overlay continuously renders frames for the blink.
fix: Use `steps(2)` or an opacity toggle.

title: Misleading comments about clip file locking ("fails quietly" and "let go of the file")
claim: Tauri's asset protocol opens files per range request (at most 1 MB) with Rust's default Windows share flags, which allow deletion, so open video elements do not lock clip files. The "let go of the file" step in save is therefore not needed for locking (only the `?v=` cache-busting is), and the console's comment that filing a clip open in the main window "fails quietly" is likely wrong: the move succeeds (see FP-11).
scenario: Developers rely on the comment and assume filing an open clip is a no-op, missing that it actually moves the file and resets the main player's trim.
fix: Correct the comments to reflect that the move succeeds.

votes.evidence: The video src comes from src/lib/ipc.ts:31-33 `convertFileSrc(path)`, i.e. Tauri's built-in `asset` protocol. The app registers no protocol of its own; src-tauri/src/lib.rs:1096 only widens the scope. ~/.cargo/registry/src/*/tauri-2.11.5/src/manager/webview.rs:343-344 registers `crate::protocol::asset::get`. tauri-2.11.5/src/protocol/asset.rs:52 `let mut file = match File::open(path.clone())` runs per request, the file is a local that is dropped when get_response returns, and :120 `const MAX_LEN: u64 = 1000 * 1024;` caps each range. wry-0.55.1 contains no SetVirtualHostNameToFolderMapping, so WebView2 never opens the file itself. Rust std's default Windows share mode is FILE_SHARE_READ|WRITE|DELETE (documented in std, but the source is not on disk here). The move path is src-tauri/src/commands.rs:745 file_clip -> filing.rs:132 `move_file(&file, &target)` -> filing.rs:272 `std::fs::rename(from, to)` with five retries, to a fresh name (free_name, so no replace). Nothing in the player holds a handle between requests, so the rename succeeds. The comment being challenged is in German at src/console/Console.tsx:747-751: `Nicht, solange sie hier läuft — das Verschieben risse die Wiedergabe ab. Spielt das Hauptfenster sie gerade, scheitert das leise` ("while the main window plays it, this fails quietly"). That comment contradicts itself: it admits a move tears the console's own playback (so the move succeeds) yet claims it fails in the main window. The guard at :752 `if (playingId !== clip.id) await api.fileClip(clip.id)` only checks the console's own player. ClipPlayer.tsx:543-544 says `The player has to let go of the file for that: Windows will not replace an open file`, and :563 says `Let go of the file: Windows will not replace a file that is still open.` The real need is at ClipPlayer.tsx:523-529: the `?v=` suffix that stops the WebView serving cached/stale ranges.
votes.corrected_claim: Accurate as stated. One nuance: the non-range path in asset.rs reads the whole file in one go. That handle is also closed when the request ends, so the conclusion holds. Detaching the element in save() is still useful: it stops new range requests against a file that is being swapped, and with them the error/'file gone' state. Its stated reason, Windows file locking, is wrong. The same misconception appears in places the finding does not list: src-tauri/src/commands.rs:739-743 (file_clip doc: 'usually because the file is still open'), src-tauri/src/filing.rs:266-267 ('the player can hold the file open ... Windows will not let go of it'), and the edit.rs:555 error text 'Is the clip open somewhere right now?'. The downstream effect (the main player reloading from the new path and losing its trim) belongs to FP-11 and was not re-verified here.
votes.reachable_by: Developers reading the comments. At runtime: a user favorites, in the console, a clip that is open in the main window's player. The file really moves and the main window's source path changes under it.
votes.fix_assessment: Rewriting the comments is correct: say that filing succeeds while the main window plays the clip, and that the player's detach exists to stop range requests and caching against a swapped file, not to release an OS lock. The behaviour itself, and whether the console should skip clips the main window is playing, needs the FP-11 fix rather than a comment change.

title: Close timeout scheduled inside a setState updater fires twice under StrictMode
claim: ClipPlayer.tsx:191-195 schedules `goodbye.current = window.setTimeout(onClose, LEAVE_MS)` inside a `setLeaving` updater function. StrictMode calls updaters twice, so in development `onClose` fires twice.

Without originOf (Dashboard) the updater also runs once eagerly at dispatch (:9143-9152) and once more in render; with originOf, setShrinking(true) at :188 queues an update first, so both calls happen in render. Either way two timeouts are scheduled with already=false, and goodbye.current (cleared on unmount at :198) holds only the second id.

The second call happens only if that timer runs before React commits. Callers are idempotent: Dashboard.tsx:276 `() => setPlaying(null)`, and Clips.tsx:327-336 closePlayer resets touched.current, so a second call files nothing. title: Hidden console keeps an infinite CSS animation (and full-screen glow layer) running for the whole session over the game
claim: When the console closes, the dock is only faded to opacity 0 by `.cb-ui[data-leaving="true"] { animation: cb-fade-out 160ms ease-in both; pointer-events: none; }` (console.css:273) and stays mounted. Console.tsx:1025 renders `<LiveDot />` in the dock whenever the buffer is running, and its ring uses `.cb-live-ring { animation: cb-live-ring 2s var(--ease-out-soft) infinite; }` (motion.css:132), so the infinite animation keeps running while the console is hidden. The window is hidden with `ShowWindow(SW_HIDE)`; Tauri's hide never calls WebView2 `SetIsVisible(false)` (only `webview.hide()` would). The console runs with `--disable-renderer-backgrounding --disable-backgrounding-occluded-windows` and `CalculateNativeWinOcclusion` off, so nothing throttles it, and with `--disable-gpu` the frames are rasterised and composited on the CPU. The full-screen `.cb-glow` layer (`will-change: opacity`) also stays alive. Related: the main window has the same flags, so any infinite animation it shows (e.g. LiveDot) also runs while it sits in the tray.
scenario: The user plays a game for hours or days with the buffer running; the hidden console's Chromium keeps producing compositor frames at about 60 fps, rasterised and composited on the CPU, while the game is in the foreground.
fix: After the exit animation (`finishClose` or `console-closed`) render an empty page instead of an invisible dock: a `visible` flag that unmounts `.cb-ui` and the glow. At minimum add `.cb-ui[data-leaving="true"] * { animation-play-state: paused }` and drop `will-change` when hidden. Optionally call `webview.hide()` from Rust after `window.hide()` and `webview.show()` before showing.

(<><LiveDot />`; LiveDot.tsx renders `cb-live-ring`; motion.css:132 `.cb-live-ring { animation: cb-live-ring 2s var(--ease-out-soft) infinite; }`; console.css:273 `.cb-ui[data-leaving="true"] { animation: cb-fade-out 160ms ease-in both; ...}` (opacity only, nothing unmounted or paused for .cb-live-ring). Console.tsx:363-391 `console-closed` only sets closing/panel state and keeps the dock mounted. lib.rs:1241 `console::create(handle);` is unconditional (open() checks console_enabled, create() does not). console.rs:71 `.additional_browser_args(overlay::BROWSER_ARGS)`; overlay.rs:53-58 the occlusion/backgrounding switches plus `--disable-gpu`. console.rs:217/230 `window.hide()` -> tauri-runtime-wry lib.rs:3490 `WindowMessage::Hide => window.set_visible(false)` -> tao window_state.rs:420-422 `ShowWindow(window, SW_HIDE)`; only the separate WebviewMessage::Hide path (tauri-runtime-wry lib.rs:3807) reaches wry webview2/mod.rs:1487 `self.controller.SetIsVisible(visible)`. wry lib.rs:819 webview attribute default `visible: true`, so the controller stays IsVisible=true for life. overlay.rs:31-38 comment: the switches exist precisely so the hidden window keeps drawing. Glow: console.css:97-98 `animation: cb-glow-in 300ms ... both; will-change: opacity;` and :114 `.cb-glow[data-leaving="true"] { animation: cb-fade-out 160ms ease-in both; }` are both finite. tauri.conf.json:27 the main window's args carry no `--disable-gpu`; NavBar.tsx:176 `<LiveDot />`.
votes.corrected_claim: The core is true: the console page keeps `<LiveDot />` mounted under an opacity-0 `.cb-ui`, so its infinite `cb-live-ring` animation keeps going while the window is hidden. Tauri's hide only calls ShowWindow(SW_HIDE) and never sets the WebView2 controller to IsVisible=false. With CalculateNativeWinOcclusion disabled and backgrounding turned off, nothing in the source would make Chromium throttle it. Four details are wrong. (1) Scope is larger than claimed: `closing` starts as true and console::create runs unconditionally at startup, so the ring runs from app launch whenever the buffer is on. This depends on Chromium/WebView2 behaviour and cannot be checked here. (3) The glow is not a per-frame cost. Its animations are finite (300 ms in, 160 ms out), so afterwards it is only a static, invisible full-screen layer that holds memory. title: Offer Accept/Decline buttons have no error handling

Neither has a catch, and src/ has no unhandledrejection handler. But src-tauri/src/share.rs:414 `pub fn share_decline(app: AppHandle, id: String) {` returns unit, so Decline never rejects. share.rs:360-370 share_accept returns Err only for `ok_or("That offer is gone.")?` or `stage != Stage::Asking => Err("That offer is no longer open.")`. {t.error}

}`.

title: `playing` stays true during save; Space calls play() on a source-less element

The rAF effect (ClipPlayer.tsx:356-378) keeps running and paints the source-less element (duration NaN, so the bar drops to 0%). The keydown handler (ClipPlayer.tsx:459-497) has no saving/restoring guard, and Space calls toggle (ClipPlayer.tsx:380-394): `if (!element.paused) {pause; return} ... void element.play();`. toggle tests element.paused, which pause() already set to true, not the `playing` state. play() on an element with no src and networkState EMPTY returns a pending promise. It is rejected with AbortError only later: on a second Space (pause()), or when the old element is removed by the `key={reload}` swap. `void` has no catch, and there is no global unhandledrejection handler, so it is only a console error.

Space calling play() during a save does not follow from `playing` staying true: toggle() checks element.paused, so Space calls play() on the source-less element whatever `playing` is. The promise does not reject at once; it stays pending until the element is paused or removed, then rejects with AbortError (unhandled, logged only). restoreOriginal() (ClipPlayer.tsx:561-587) has the same path. It is a little worse there: resumeAt.playing is false, so pause() in onLoadedMetadata on an already paused new element may fire no pause event, and `playing` can stay true after the restore (this part depends on runtime timing).
votes.reachable_by: A user pressing Space/K during a save or restore, or saving/restoring while the clip plays. That gives a stale play icon, a brief rAF loop and a bar jump; a console-only rejection follows.
votes.fix_assessment: `setPlaying(false)` in save()/restoreOriginal() fixes the stale flag and the rAF loop but does not stop Space from calling play(). Also make toggle/the keydown handler return while `saving || restoring` (or when the element has no src), and add `.catch(() => {})` to play().

title: Overlay timer cleanup clears the initial array, not the current timers
claim: Overlay.tsx:112-115 `const running = timers.current; ... running.forEach(clearTimeout)` captures the initial array, so on cleanup it clears that array rather than the timers that later replaced it.
scenario: On unmount, pending banner timers that were stored in a replaced array are not cleared and still fire.
fix: Clear `timers.current` at cleanup time (read the ref when cleaning up).

votes.evidence: src/overlay/Overlay.tsx:71-72 `timers.current.forEach(clearTimeout); timers.current = [];` runs before every push (:78-84), so the array captured at :112 `const running = timers.current;` never holds a timer, and cleanup :115 `running.forEach(clearTimeout)` clears nothing. However, Overlay is the root of its own window (src/overlay/main.tsx:12-16 `createRoot(...).render(<React.StrictMode><Overlay /></React.StrictMode>)`) and is never conditionally rendered anywhere else, so the effect cleanup runs only on StrictMode's dev re-mount at startup (before any banner, when there are no timers) or when the window is torn down.
votes.corrected_claim: The cleanup really reads a stale, always-empty array, so it is dead code. But no scenario shows the symptom: the component never unmounts while banner timers are pending, except at window teardown, where the timers die with the page. Even if it did, setLeaving or setBanner on an unmounted component is a silent no-op in React 19. This is a code smell, not a user-visible bug.
votes.reachable_by: Not reachable in a way anyone can observe; at most a dev HMR re-run of the effect, where the old timers just finish the banner on the same still-mounted component.
votes.fix_assessment: Reading timers.current at cleanup time (and silencing the exhaustive-deps lint rule there) is correct and harmless, but the gain is purely hygienic.

title: Whole Console tree re-renders on every 1 Hz status event, even while hidden
claim: The whole Console tree re-renders on every `engine-status`, `audio-errors` and `audio-warnings` event (1 Hz each, always fresh objects), including while hidden (Console.tsx:349-353, Trouble.tsx:41-42).
scenario: While the user plays, the hidden console re-renders three times a second for no visible change.
fix: Compare payloads before calling setState, or skip while `hidden.current`.

votes.evidence: lib.rs:1065-1084 `if tick % 20 == 0 { ... handle.emit("engine-status", status); handle.emit("audio-errors", state.audio.errors()); ... handle.emit("audio-warnings", warnings);` (tick = 50 ms, lib.rs:944, so 1 Hz each). Console.tsx:349-353 `listen<EngineStatus>("engine-status", (e) => { setStatus(e.payload); trendPush(e.payload); })` with no hidden check; Trouble.tsx:41-42 `setErrors(e.payload)` / `setWarnings(e.payload)` with fresh deserialized objects, so React's Object.is bail-out never fires. Trend.tsx:64 `setSamples((prev) => prev.concat(...).slice(-TREND_SECONDS))` lives in Console (Console.tsx:235) and is meant to run while hidden (Trend.tsx:11-14: 'auch an das versteckte. Die Konsole sammelt also weiter, während sie zu ist'). tauri-2.11.5 webview/mod.rs:1974 emit_js -> one `self.eval(...)` per emit, so each event is its own script task.
votes.corrected_claim: Console re-renders at least once a second while hidden, and up to three times a second. It is 1-3 times because the three emits are separate eval tasks, and React 19 batches them only if its scheduler task has not run between them. The engine-status render is unavoidable with the current design: useTrend's setSamples (state held in Console) must update every second while hidden on purpose, and the status changes every tick anyway. Only the audio-errors/audio-warnings setStates are avoidable, since they usually carry an unchanged `{}`. While hidden, panel and playingId are null, so what re-renders is the dock, the TroubleStrip and Offers, not a large tree.
votes.reachable_by: Always, from app start: the console page is created hidden at startup (lib.rs:1241 console::create) and gets the 1 Hz broadcasts for the whole session.
votes.fix_assessment: The 'skip while hidden.current' option would break the intended trend collection if applied to trendPush, and applied to setStatus alone it saves nothing because setSamples re-renders Console anyway. Comparing the audio maps before setErrors/setWarnings (or moving the trend buffer into a ref) is the part that actually helps.

title: Offers cannot distinguish same-named friends and do not strip bidi characters
claim: Offers show only `friendName` (taken from the local friend list) with no avatar, so two friends with the same display name cannot be told apart. The sender controls `t.name` and `t.game`, and bidi control characters are not stripped.
scenario: A friend sends a file whose name uses bidi control characters to disguise its extension, or two friends share a name and the user accepts from the wrong one.
fix: Show an avatar; strip bidi control characters from sender-controlled fields.

votes.evidence: src/console/Offers.tsx:38-44 renders only `${t.friendName} wants to send you ${what}` and `{t.name} · {megabytes(t.size)}{t.game && ...}`, with no avatar or username. friendName comes from the local list, src-tauri/src/friends.rs:627-631 `.map(|user| user.display_name.clone())`, and display names are not unique (FriendUser has a separate `username`, src/lib/types.ts:288-293). share.rs:558 `let name = meta.title.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| meta.file_name.clone());` and share.rs:578 `game: meta.game.clone()` are sender-controlled and shown unfiltered (also in src/components/Share.tsx:311-312). However, the file actually written is `safe_file_name(&meta.file_name)` (share.rs:643). safe_file_name (share.rs:1176-1197) cuts any path, replaces `is_control()` characters (Cc only, so bidi Cf characters survive) and forces the extension to `mp4|mkv|mov|webm|png|jpg|jpeg`, falling back to `mp4`. The in-game banner does pass the avatar (share.rs:602 `crate::friends::friend_avatar(app, from)`).
votes.corrected_claim: The console offer card identifies the sender only by display name, so two friends with the same display name cannot be told apart there (the in-game banner does show the avatar). Sender-controlled `name` (title or file name) and `game` are shown without stripping bidi controls. The 'disguise its extension' risk is moot: the saved file always gets an allowlisted media extension, and the sender can put any misleading text in the title without bidi tricks. The impact is cosmetic or confusion only.
votes.reachable_by: Any accepted friend: they control their own display name and the offer's title, file name and game fields.
votes.fix_assessment: Showing the avatar (friend_avatar is already available via friendId) or the username in the Offer card fixes the ambiguity cheaply. Stripping U+202A-202E and U+2066-2069 from name and game is cheap hardening, but it does not close a real file-type spoofing hole.

title: Custom CSS properties require repeated `as CSSProperties` casts
claim: Inline styles setting custom CSS properties need `as CSSProperties` casts throughout; one typed helper would do.
scenario: Casts hide type errors in style objects.
fix: Add one typed helper for custom CSS properties.

votes.evidence: Exactly five casts in three files, each on a style object that holds only custom properties: src/components/ui/BusyVeil.tsx:109 `({ "--cb-head": `${clamp(shown) * 100}%` } as CSSProperties)`; src/overlay/Overlay.tsx:188 and :204 `{ "--cb-stroke": stroke } as CSSProperties`; Overlay.tsx:317 `{ "--cb-stroke": asks ? ... } as CSSProperties`; src/console/Console.tsx:929-933 `{ "--cb-scale": String(scale), "--inset": `${bottomInset}px` } as React.CSSProperties`. The casts are needed: node_modules/@types/react (19.2.18) index.d.ts:2486-2489 `interface CSSProperties extends CSS.Properties<string | number> { /** The index signature was removed ... You're able to use type assertion or module augmentation`. A scratch tsc 5.9.3 run showed `{ color: 5, "--x": "a" } as CSSProperties` still fails with TS2352 (`number` is not comparable to `Color`), while `{ colr: "red" } as CSSProperties` passes. No d.ts augments CSSProperties (src/vite-env.d.ts is the only d.ts).
votes.corrected_claim: There are five `as CSSProperties` casts in three files (BusyVeil, Overlay x3, Console), so "throughout" overstates it. The casts are required by @types/react's closed CSSProperties type. They do not switch off type checking: a wrong value type on a standard property is still rejected (TS2352). They only let misspelled or extra keys through. All five objects contain nothing but `--*` keys, so no type error is hidden today. This is a style nit.
votes.reachable_by: Developers only. A future edit that adds a misspelled standard CSS key to one of these five style objects would compile without a warning. There is no runtime or user impact.
votes.fix_assessment: A helper function would still need a cast inside it. The idiomatic fix that the @types/react comment itself suggests is a one-time module augmentation (`declare module "react" { interface CSSProperties { [key: `--${string}`]: string | number } }` in src/vite-env.d.ts). That removes all five casts and keeps excess-property checks on standard keys.

title: Optimistic deleteClip never rolls back on failure
claim: store.ts:484 `deleteClip` removes the clip from the store optimistically and never rolls back if `api.deleteClip` throws, so the clip disappears from the UI but stays on disk and in the database until the next reload.
scenario: `delete_clip` fails (e.g. file in use); the clip vanishes from the gallery but is still on disk and in the DB, reappearing after reload.
fix: Roll back `deleteClip` on failure and show the error.

title: Stems are not paused while the video is seeking
claim: useClipMix does not pause the stem `<audio>` elements on the video's `seeking` event, so audio from the old position keeps playing until `seeked`.
scenario: User seeks during playback and hears audio from the previous position until the seek completes.
fix: Pause the stems on `seeking`.

title: Single-track clips: track gain and mute have no audible preview but are saved
claim: useClipMix.ts:128 `const separate = tracks.length > 1 && ...`; the audio-elements effect returns early when not separate, and useClipMix.ts:280 sets `video.current.volume = separate ? 0 : master;`. With one track, ClipEditor still renders a TrackRow (mute, solo, -30...+12 dB); moving it changes nothing in the preview, but Save bakes it into the file.
scenario: User with a single-track clip raises the track to +12 dB, hears no change, saves, and the exported file is unexpectedly louder/clipped.
fix: Apply the single track's gain to the video element (attenuation via `volume`, or route the video through the same WebAudio graph for boost), or hide the row.

title: Waveform is not refreshed after a trim and is misaligned with the new timeline

fix: Add `reload` (or `clip.sizeBytes`) to the dependencies and append `?v=${clip.sizeBytes}`, as is already done for thumbnails.

title: Frame step is hard-coded to 30 fps
claim: ClipPlayer.tsx:59 `const FRAME = 1 / 30;` is used at line 478 `".": () => seek(FRAME)`. Recordings default to 60 fps, so a "single frame" step moves two frames.
scenario: User frame-steps a 60 fps clip with `.` and skips every other frame, making precise cuts impossible.
fix: Carry fps in `Clip`, or derive it from `requestVideoFrameCallback` metadata.

title: Trim marks and the selection loop use currentTime instead of the presented frame
claim: Marks set while playing take `currentTime` (the audio clock), not the presented frame, and the end-of-selection loop check uses rAF plus `currentTime`.
scenario: User sets an out-mark while playing; the mark lands on a different time than the frame visible on screen.
fix: Use `rVFC.mediaTime` (requestVideoFrameCallback) for marks and for the end-of-selection loop check instead of rAF plus `currentTime`.

title: Time display and trim readout show whole seconds only
claim: PlayerControls.tsx:15 `clock()` floors to seconds, and ClipEditor shows `clock(trim.start) – clock(trim.end)`, so the handle tooltip and trim readout cannot show the sub-second precision a cut needs.
scenario: User adjusts a trim by 300 ms; the readout does not change, so the user cannot tell where the cut is.
fix: Display m:ss.cc or frames.

title: Export dialog: shown size can differ from the exported target size

Typing "0.5" keeps the previous 25 MB target while the field shows 0.5. Typing "7" and then clearing the field leaves `targetMb = 7` with no preset highlighted and an empty field, yet Export is enabled.
scenario: User types 0.5 MB and clicks Export; a 25 MB file is produced.
fix: Derive `targetMb` from `custom` when it is non-empty and disable Export for invalid input.

title: Export cannot be cancelled
claim: There is no way to cancel a long export: Cancel is disabled while busy, and Rust has no cancel command.
scenario: User starts a long export by mistake and has to wait for it to finish.
fix: Add a cancel that kills ffmpeg.

title: Export uses the file on disk, not the unsaved selection, without saying so
claim: ExportDialog exports the file on disk, not the unsaved trim selection, and does not tell the user.
scenario: User sets a trim (unsaved) and exports a copy; the export contains the full untrimmed clip.
fix: Add a hint when `dirty`.

title: Player keeps reacting behind the Export dialog and the dialog follows the player's clip
claim: While ExportDialog is open, `n`/`p` still page the player. ExportDialog's `clip` prop follows the player's clip, so mid-run the dialog shows the next clip's numbers and the progress stalls.
scenario: User starts an export and presses `n`; the dialog switches to the next clip's info and the progress bar stops updating.
fix: Capture the clip at mount.

title: Usage stats are on by default and a self-dismissing notice counts as consent
claim: config.rs:66 `usage_stats: true`; Setup.tsx:88 `useState(true)` then line 113 `setUsageStats(config.usageStats)` - a pre-ticked toggle on the last setup step. UsageNotice marks itself as read after 10 s with the window focused: `if (due && shownMs >= SHOWN_MS) void patchConfig({ usageStatsNoticed: true })`. telemetry.rs `send_if_due` sends a persistent UUID `id` plus `source` and `heard`. claim: The UsageNotice text ("the version, how many clips, which features. No content, no account.") does not mention that telemetry.rs `send_if_due` sends a persistent install UUID `id` and the attribution fields `source` and `heard`.

claim: In Console.tsx:1314-1340 the `

title: ClipPlayer, ExportDialog and SharePicker have no dialog role or focus management

title: Overlay capability `core:event:default` lets the overlay emit events to the main window
claim: overlay.json grants `"permissions": ["core:event:default"]` with the description "only listens, controls nothing". `core:event:default` includes `allow-emit` and `allow-emit-to`, so the overlay can send `share-state`, `focus-clip`, `update-available` or `main-hidden` to the main window.

title: Console capability grants unused window permissions and broad `core:default`
claim: The console capability grants `core:window:allow-hide/show/set-focus`, which its JavaScript never uses, and `core:default` (tray, menu and more).
scenario: Script in the console webview can manipulate windows, the tray or menus beyond what the console needs.

title: Player's global key handler ignores menus/dialogs and hijacks keys on sliders
claim: ClipPlayer.tsx:463-469 skips only text inputs, deliberately not range sliders: `(target instanceof HTMLInputElement && target.type !== "range") || target instanceof HTMLTextAreaElement`. Line 499 looks up `handlers[event.key]` without checking `event.defaultPrevented` or modifier keys; line 492's Escape only respects `askingDelete` and `exporting`. Conflicts: the context menu (Menu.tsx:156) handles Escape and arrows in the capture phase with `preventDefault` but no `stopPropagation`, so Escape closes the menu and the player, and ArrowDown moves the menu selection and lowers the volume. SharePicker (Share.tsx:36), opened from the player's menu, closes on Escape and so does the player; Space, `n`, `p` act on the player behind it. ClipEditor's "Free up space" ConfirmDelete (`discarding`, ClipEditor.tsx:84) cancels on Escape and the player closes too. With a track-gain or volume slider focused, ArrowLeft/Right seek +/-5 s and ArrowUp/Down change master volume, so keyboard users cannot move any slider; Home/End are taken too. scenario: User opens the context menu in the player and presses Escape: both the menu and the player close. User focuses a track-gain slider and presses ArrowRight: the video seeks +5 s instead of the slider moving.

title: mark() does not clamp the end to duration and silently moves the start
claim: `mark()` (ClipPlayer.tsx:451-455) does not clamp the end to the duration (`Math.max(at, current.start + 0.5)`), and silently moves the start to `end - 0.5` when the playhead is past it.
scenario: User marks an end near the clip's end with start close by; the end can exceed duration, or the start silently shifts.
fix: Clamp the end to `[start + 0.5, duration]`.

votes.evidence: src/components/ClipPlayer.tsx:447-456 `const at = element.currentTime; setTrim(current => which === "start" ? { start: Math.min(at, current.end - 0.5), end: current.end } : { start: current.start, end: Math.max(at, current.start + 0.5) });`. `at` is currentTime, which is at most the duration. Every setter keeps start <= end - 0.5 <= duration - 0.5: mark start (above), the Scrubber drag `start: Math.min(at, trim.end - 0.5)` (PlayerControls.tsx:150-153), Reset `{ start: 0, end: duration }` (ClipEditor.tsx:150), and restoreTrim of a core-written edit, which is always `{0, applied.duration_ms}` (commands.rs:1327-1331). So `Math.max(at, start + 0.5)` cannot exceed the duration. mark('end') never touches the start (`start: current.start`).
votes.corrected_claim: The end cannot exceed the duration through mark(), because all trim setters keep start at most duration - 0.5. The only exceptions are degenerate: a clip shorter than 0.5 s, or a hand-made or legacy edit whose start sits in the last 0.5 s. Even then the core clamps the end to the clip length (edit.rs:281) and the bar clamps to 100% (PlayerControls.tsx `percent`), so only the time readout would be off. The "start moves" part is the deliberate 0.5 s minimum-length clamp: 'Start here' with the playhead past end - 0.5 places the start at end - 0.5, and the readout shows the new times (ClipEditor.tsx:162). That is a UX choice, not a defect.
votes.reachable_by: Not reachable in normal use. It needs a clip shorter than 0.5 s or a stored start in the last 0.5 s of the file.
votes.fix_assessment: Clamping the end to [start + 0.5, duration] is harmless defensive code but fixes nothing reachable. If the start clamp should change, pushing the end out (or swapping the marks) would be a UX decision, not a bug fix.

title: Slider has no focus ring
claim: The Slider uses `outline-none` (Controls.tsx:116), so there is no visible focus ring.
scenario: Keyboard users cannot see which slider is focused.
fix: Add a visible focus style.

also.title: Thickness slider has no visible focus
also.claim: The slider control in Controls.tsx (91-124, 109-120) uses `outline-none`, so there is no visible focus indicator.

votes.evidence: src/index.css:64-67 defines an unlayered `:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-accent); outline-offset: 2px; }`. Tailwind v4 (node_modules/tailwindcss 4.3.3) puts `outline-none` (`--tw-outline-style:none; outline-style:none`) in `@layer utilities`. The compiled dist/assets/accent-CTvuYMT0.css confirms it: `.outline-none{...}` sits inside `@layer utilities` and `:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--color-accent);outline-offset:2px}` sits at top level. Under the cascade-layers rules, unlayered normal declarations beat layered ones whatever their specificity. So when the Slider (Controls.tsx:116) gets keyboard focus, it still draws the 2px accent ring. No other compiled rule in the main or console CSS resets outline. index.css is imported by all three entry points (src/main.tsx:4, src/console/main.tsx:4, src/overlay/main.tsx:4). The same applies to the merged EF-24 (the ShotViewer thickness slider uses the same Slider).

votes.fix_assessment: No fix needed. Removing `outline-none` would be harmless cleanup, but it changes nothing for keyboard users.

title: backdrop-blur in the transparent GPU-less console costs CPU and blurs nothing
claim: `backdrop-blur` is used inside the transparent, `--disable-gpu` console (Console.tsx:642, Friends.tsx:157). It costs CPU and, as overlay.css itself notes, blurs nothing behind the window.

fix: Remove `backdrop-blur` from the console.

Console.tsx:635-642: the blur sits on a 40x40 hover pill inside a clip tile, over the tile's own thumbnail: `` then ``. Friends.tsx:157 SendTo is `absolute inset-0 ... bg-black/85 p-2 backdrop-blur-md`, placed over a clip tile (`
`, Console.tsx:631). The overlay.css:154-159 / console.css:231-234 notes are about full-surface backgrounds (`.cb-card`, `.cb-glass`) whose only backdrop is the transparent window. That is a different situation.

They are small (a 40x40 pill shown only on hover; a tile-sized overlay shown only while 'Send to' is open) and short-lived, not a cost of opening the console. At most it is a nit that the SendTo blur under 85% black is barely visible.

title: Fake RESTING mock status is the console's initial state in production
claim: Console.tsx:54-69 defines a `RESTING` mock status (`game: "ARC Raiders"`, 96 s buffered) that is used as the initial state in production too.
scenario: On first open before the real status arrives, the console shows "ARC Raiders" and 96 s buffered regardless of reality.
fix: Use null and a skeleton.

votes.evidence: Console.tsx:52-53 documents RESTING as the pre-core placeholder for `npm run dev`. In the app it never reaches the screen. (1) The console page loads at startup into a hidden window (console.rs:54-55 'Create the console window, hidden.
